response.sql: WITH sex_counts AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS test_records FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.SEX), totals AS (SELECT AVG(test_records) AS average_per_sex, SUM(test_records) AS total_records FROM sex_counts) SELECT s.sex, s.test_records, 1.0 * s.test_records / t.total_records AS share_of_total, s.test_records - t.average_per_sex AS above_average FROM sex_counts AS s CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE s.test_records > t.average_per_sex

assumptions.assumption: Patients with NULL sex are excluded from the sex breakdown, average, and total.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat NULL sex as an unknown-sex group and include its records in the average and total.
